Presuming that the term "interaction" refers to how we communicate with them, then it is a rather complicated situation.

I have one cat, and one dog. So, this is how it works with us. Both of them have established specific ways in which they interact with us. But for the most part, it seems to be that our cat will address situations that are incredibly important, while our dog will only address situations that are not important at all. If the cat bowl runs out of food (ahem, because our dog stole all of it), our cat will most certainly let us know. She will come up to you, sit, and just stare at you until you become so uncomfortable that you realize she's saying: "Um, I require food and water, immediately!" Also, because she likes to destroy furniture, we'll often say her name when she starts digging her claws into the couch, to which the little convict will reply: "Who? Me?" -- in fact, if you say anything to her, she'll verbally respond in some way, often saying things like: "What? I wasn't doing anything! I promise!" And even though she will verbally respond, she still won't do anything you want her to do. We like to say she's "independent." Now, our dog on the other hand... she's very carefree and she's in love with my wife. When my wife walks through the door, she'll go bananas, shouting, "Oh-em-gee! Oh-em-gee! You're home, you're home, you're home, you're home, you're home! I've waited all day for you! You are amazing! Oh, you're so wonderful! Did I tell you that you're amazing? And you're home, you're home, you're home!" If she goes outside, she'll watch the traffic on the road, and as soon as she sees someone on a bicycle, she'll tell you about it: "Hey! Hey! That guy's riding a bicycle! Hey! Did you see him? He's riding a bicycle!" Yes, we see him, and it's not a big deal. What's with you and bicycles, anyway? Weirdo.

So, the answer, I suppose, is no. Cats interact with humans just as much as dogs interact with humans. But, apparently, for very different reasons.
